Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Order

The appellant was respondent No. 3 in a claim petition filed on file No. 23/MACT of 2014 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Samba which came to award compensation in favour of the claimants/respondents No. 2 to 5 amounting to Rs. 9,13,750/- along with interest made payable by the respondent No. 1 - New India Assurance Company Ltd. with a right reserved in favour of the respondent No. 1 - New India Assurance Company Ltd., to recover it from the owner of the offending vehicle who is the appellant herein and that is how the appellant is in the present appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
02. Mr. Jugal Kishore Gupta, learned counsel for the respondent No. 1 - New India Assurance Company Ltd. causes his appearance.

03. On behalf of the respondents No. 2 to 5, their services by deemed mode have taken place and otherwise also their presence is not of that much importance as they are not in any contest in the Rajesh Sharma vs New India Assurance on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94234860/

04.

However, respondent No. 6 - Vikas Sharma, the driver of the offending vehicle against whom also the respondent No. 1 - Insurance Company has also been reserved right to recover along with appellant is reported to have expired as per office noting dated 22.09.2023.
05. Let appellant take appropriate steps by reference to disclosure of the fact that the respondent No. 6 - Vikas Sharma has demised.

06. List along with main matter on 23.10.2024.
07.

In the meantime, the respondent No. 1/non-applicant No. 1 to respond the application CM No.
5434/2023 seeking condonation of delay in maintaining the present appeal.

(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 11.09.2024 Bunty Rajesh Sharma vs New India Assurance on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94234860/
